subject: Pilot packaging: phased commit + 45-day conversion window
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Akhil Khan <akhan@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-06-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot packaging: phased commit + 45-day conversion window

Hi Akhil,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion. Per our conversation I wanted to put a concrete pilot packaging option on the table that balances runway for your engineering evaluation with clear paths to conversion. High-level proposal attached (Acme_POCPricing_v1.pdf). Key points below: 

- 30-day free evaluation credits to validate core flows (month 0)
- Phased commit: if you opt to convert we convert to a 3-month committed slab with graduated discounts; if not converted you can take a 45-day conversion window from the end of the pilot to sign the commit.
- Month 2 discount (if conversion happens at conversion event): 55% off published hosted rate for the committed slab (tiered by usage).
- Engineering hours: 40 hours of onboarding & performance support included during the pilot (sprint-style).
- SLA: standard Redwood pilot SLA; uplift options available if you choose a Dedicated sandbox (add-on).
- Carryover: up to 20% of unused pilot credits can be converted into the first month of committed usage.

Questions for you: does the 45-day conversion window sound workable, and would you prefer conversion to be automatic on signature or require a separate activation?

If this looks good I can route internally for a one-time concessions approval and send a DocuSign LOI to lock things in.

Best,
Dev Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Acme_POCPricing_v1.pdf

From: Akhil Khan <akhan@acme.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-29T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging: phased commit + 45-day conversion window

Dev — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few immediate asks from our side: 

1) Conversion window: can we stretch to 60 days? Our security review & procurement timeline is tight.
2) Discount: to justify the lift internally, can you land month-2 at 60% off rather than 55%?
3) Sandbox: we need a dedicated sandbox for the PoC (with isolation) — what pricing/ops tradeoffs exist?
4) Credits carryover: would prefer at least 30% carryover into month-1 of committed usage.

Also tagging procurement (procurement@acme.ai) — they will want invoicing cadence and a draft SOW. Do you have an SLA addendum we can review?

Thanks — Akhil
VP, Product | Acme AI

My read: Acme is strategic and likely to convert, but procurement timeline is real. I can push back on the 60% discount but we should consider a trade (e.g., fewer eng hours, SLA only on Dedicated, or tighter carryover). What's acceptable to push to the customer?

Dev — thanks for the context. My recommendation:

- Do NOT give 60% off; cap at 55% for month-2 but make it conditional on a signed LOI within the 60-day window (we can meet halfway on timing).
- Offer 30 engineering hours instead of 40 as the base; add a paid block of hours for faster turnaround (we can discount those).
- Sandbox: Dedicated sandbox is fine as an add-on at cost + a small one-time setup fee; do not include uplifted SLA for hosted pilot — reserve SLA uplift for Dedicated.
- Carryover: 25% max; 30% is too generous.
- Add a one-time invoice credit of $2,500 if they sign the LOI by EOW to accelerate procurement.

If marketing/legal need to sign the concession, I'm comfortable with the above.

Ben
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot packaging: phased commit + 45-day conversion window

Ben's suggestions look good. Additional option to present to Acme as an alternative (sell the choice):

Option A (Discount-first):
- 45% off month-2 + 30% carryover + 30 eng hrs included + 45-day conversion window

Option B (Commit-first):
- Tiered 3-month committed slab at 30% off published rate with a 30-day conversion window, up to 25% carryover, and a one-time performance tuning sprint (8 hours) included; SLA uplift offered only on Dedicated sandbox.

Rationale: giving them a choice frames us as flexible and protects list price. If they push for 60% we can surface Option B as a lower-discount but commitment-first alternative they can present to procurement.

Also attach SLA addendum draft and a redline of your pricing sheet before sending externally (Attachment: Acme_POCPricing_v1_redline.pdf, SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx).

-Kimberly

Akhil — thanks for the candid asks and for looping procurement. After internal review we can do the following counteroffer: 

Counteroffer (best-effort compromise):
- Conversion window: 45 days from pilot end (we can extend to 60 days only with an LOI that outlines the commitment-to-sign timeline).
- Month-2 discount: 55% off hosted rate if LOI is signed within 30 days; otherwise 50% if signed within the 45-day window.
- Carryover: up to 25% of unused pilot credits converted into the first committed month.
- Engineering hours: 30 hours included during the pilot plus a one-time performance tuning sprint (8 hours) upon conversion.
- Dedicated sandbox: available as an add-on; estimate provided separately (one-time setup fee + hourly infra surcharge). SLA uplift applies only to Dedicated.
- Signing incentive: $2,500 invoice credit if LOI returned by 2026-07-08.

I've attached the redlined pricing and a draft SLA addendum for your legal/procurement review (Acme_POCPricing_v1_redline.pdf, SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx). If this addresses procurement timelines we can send a short LOI (DocuSign link: https://redwood.ai/ds/12345) to lock the special pricing.
